title: How can we help wild bees?
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Beth. Do you like honey, Phil?
sentences.zh: 我是菲尔 我是贝丝 你喜欢蜂蜜吗 菲尔

sentences.en: Hmm, I use it a lot in cooking, so yes. Well, the relationship between humans, honey and the bees which make it goes back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我经常用它做饭,所以是的 人类,蜂蜜和蜜蜂之间的关系

sentences.en: Prized for its taste and medicinal properties, in ancient times honey was known as 'liquid gold'.
sentences.zh: 在古代,蜂蜜因其品味和药用特性而获奖,被称为“液态黄金”。

sentences.en: But now, thanks to modern farming methods, populations of many insects, including bees, are in decline.
sentences.zh: 但是,由于现代耕作方法,包括蜜蜂在内的许多昆虫的数量正在减少。

sentences.en: Saoirse, a worried listener from London, called BBC World Service programme CrowdScience about the problem.
sentences.zh: 英国广播公司世界服务节目Crowd Science,

sentences.en: I'm Saoirse from the UK and my question is: can honey help save bees?
sentences.zh: 我是英国的赛尔莎,我的问题是:蜂蜜能救蜜蜂吗?

sentences.en: I've been vegan for about nine years and I don't eat honey myself, but I still have a question mark around it because I know that our bee populations are declining.
sentences.zh: 我素食了九年 自己不吃蜂蜜 但我还有个问题 因为我知道蜜蜂数量在下降

sentences.en: Saoirse is a vegan – someone who doesn't eat anything which comes from animals.
sentences.zh: 赛尔斯是个素食主义者,不吃动物的东西。

sentences.en: Not just meat, but things like milk, eggs and honey too.
sentences.zh: 不只是肉,还有牛奶、鸡蛋和蜂蜜

sentences.en: Although Saoirse doesn't eat honey herself, she says there's a question mark around eating honey.
sentences.zh: 虽然赛尔莎自己不吃蜂蜜 她说吃蜂蜜时有个问题

sentences.en: The phrase a question mark around something means there's doubt or uncertainty about something.
sentences.zh: 围绕某事的问号 意味着对某事有怀疑或不确定

sentences.en: And what Saoirse is uncertain about is whether eating honey might actually save bees.
sentences.zh: 赛尔斯不确定的是 吃蜜蜂是否真的能拯救蜜蜂

sentences.en: So, would it be better for declining bee populations if more people ate honey?
sentences.zh: 所以,如果更多的人吃蜂蜜,对减少蜜蜂数量来说会更好吗?

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing, using some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们将要讨论的, 使用一些有用的新词和短语。

sentences.en: Plus, you'll find all the vocabulary from this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 此外,你会在我们的网站上 找到这集的词汇,bbc学习英语。 com。

sentences.en: But bee-fore that I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 不过我有个问题要问你 菲尔

sentences.en: The buzzing sound bees are famous for is made by flapping their four wings incredibly fast, but how fast?
sentences.zh: 蜂鸣声是出名的 因为它的四翼拍打 速度惊人之快,但有多快?

sentences.en: Do honey bees flap their wings: a) 90 times per second, b) 190 times per second, or c) 290 times per second?
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂有没有拍翅膀:(a) 每秒90次,(b) 每秒190次,或(c) 每秒290次?

sentences.en: Well, I have absolutely no idea, so I'm going to guess 190 times per second.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我完全不知道, 所以我要去猜测 190次每秒。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧 我们稍后在节目里会找出答案的

sentences.en: We've been talking about honey bees, but these are just one of the 20,000 species of bee which exist around the world.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在谈论蜜蜂, 但这些只是全世界存在的20,000种蜜蜂之一。

sentences.en: In fact, honey bees are one of the most widespread insects on the planet and not endangered at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上,蜜蜂是地球上最普遍的昆虫之一,根本没有濒临灭绝。

sentences.en: But the picture isn't so good for wild bees, including the bumble bee, as biologist Dave Goulson, from the University of Sussex, explained to BBC World Service programme CrowdScience:
sentences.zh: 这张照片对野蜜蜂来说不太好, 包括小蜜蜂, 由苏塞克斯大学的生物学家Dave Goulson向英国广播公司世界服务节目Crowd Science解释:

sentences.en: In the UK, we have 26 bumblebee species but three have gone extinct.
sentences.zh: 在英国,我们有26个大黄蜂物种,但有3个已经灭绝。

sentences.en: Many of the others are now clinging on in little isolated pockets of good habitat.
sentences.zh: 许多其他人现在则生活在一些孤立的好栖息地。

sentences.en: Honey bees have beekeepers to look after them, but nobody's looking out for the wild bees.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂有养蜂人照顾他们 但没人照顾野蜜蜂

sentences.en: Three of the 26 species of British bumblebee have gone extinct, and Dave says other species are clinging on, meaning barely continuing to survive with great effort.
sentences.zh: 26种英国大黄蜂中的3种已经灭绝, 戴夫说其他物种正在紧紧抓住, 意思是勉强继续 以巨大的努力生存。

sentences.en: This happens in isolated pockets – small areas of habitat in which a particular insect or animal can survive.
sentences.zh: 这发生在孤立的地块上 — — 一种特定的昆虫或动物能够生存的小生境地区。

sentences.en: So, while honey bees may not be endangered, lots of other bee species are, and this is bad news because we rely on insects to pollinate crops and to keep ecosystems functioning.
sentences.zh: 因此,虽然蜜蜂可能不会濒危, 许多其他蜜蜂物种也会濒临灭绝, 这是坏消息, 因为我们依靠昆虫来授粉作物, 维持生态系统的运作。

sentences.en: That's right, Beth. 87% of all plant species need insects for pollination, so without them most plants on Earth would disappear, which would obviously be catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 没错 贝丝 87%的植物需要昆虫授粉 所以没有昆虫 地球上的大多数植物都会消失 这显然是灾难性的

sentences.en: But according to Dave Goulson, pollination is just one of the many things bees do for us, as he explained to BBC World Service's CrowdScience: That isn't the only thing that insects are doing and there are much less glamorous, less well-known things, like recycling cow poo and helping to keep the soil healthy and helping to control crop pests and so on, all of which are also really important.
sentences.zh: 但根据Dave Goulson的说法,授粉只是许多蜜蜂为我们做的事情之一,正如他向英国广播公司世界服务社的《人群科学》所解释的那样:这不是昆虫正在做的唯一的事情,而且有更不光彩、更不为人知的事情,例如回收牛粪和帮助保持土壤健康,以及帮助控制作物虫害等等,所有这些都非常重要。

sentences.en: And we, kind of, take them for granted or are just oblivious that they're even happening.
sentences.zh: 我们,有点, 认为他们是理所当然的 或者只是忽视 他们甚至正在发生。

sentences.en: Recycling cow poo and keeping the soil healthy are two important jobs bees do which we take for granted.
sentences.zh: 回收牛粪和保持土壤健康是两项重要工作,我们认为这是理所当然的。

sentences.en: If you take something for granted, you fail to value or appreciate something which benefits you.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为某事是理所当然的, 你没有价值 或欣赏的东西 对你有好处。

sentences.en: We humans are oblivious, meaning unaware or unmindful of the many things bees do to support life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 我们人类是盲目的, 意指不知道 或不关心很多事情 蜜蜂做支持 地球上的生命。

sentences.en: So, while eating more honey probably won't do much to save wild bees, there are things you can do, such as growing bee-friendly plants which flower in spring, like lavender.
sentences.zh: 所以,虽然吃更多的蜂蜜 可能不会做什么 拯救野生蜜蜂, 但有些事情你可以做, 例如生长蜂爱植物 花在春天, 像熏衣草。

sentences.en: OK. Phil, I think it's time to reveal the answer to my question.
sentences.zh: 好吧,菲尔,我想是时候 揭示答案我的问题。

sentences.en: I asked you how many times bees flap their wings per second.
sentences.zh: 我问你,多少次蜜蜂 拍翅膀每秒。

sentences.en: You said 190, which was… the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 你说190,这是... 正确的答案。

sentences.en: Well done! Ooh! OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with vegan – someone who doesn't consume any animal products.
sentences.zh: 做得好!好吧,让我们总结一下我们学到的词汇,从素食开始 — — 一个不消费任何动物产品的人。

sentences.en: If you say there's a question mark around something, you mean there's some doubt or uncertainty about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你说在某事上有一个问题标记, 你的意思是,对它有一些怀疑或不确定。

sentences.en: If an animal species is clinging on, it's holding on to existence with great effort.
sentences.zh: 如果一个动物物种 紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧紧地紧紧抓住着它的存在

sentences.en: Isolated pockets refer to small areas of habitat in which a particular insect or animal can survive.
sentences.zh: 孤立的口袋是指某一昆虫或动物能够生存的小型生境地区。

sentences.en: To take something for granted means to not appreciate or show gratitude for something which helps you.
sentences.zh: 接受一些理所当然的东西 意味着不欣赏 或表示感激的东西 帮助你。

sentences.en: And finally, the adjective oblivious means unaware.
sentences.zh: 最后,这个形容词 隐蔽意味着不知道。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you're keen for more then head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, and download the worksheet and try the quiz on this episode.
sentences.zh: 再次,我们的六分钟已经到了, 但如果你热衷于更多的话, 那就去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 然后下载工作表, 并尝试这个插曲的测试。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now. Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见,再见!
